harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a persistent ufw host firewall on node1 (Ubuntu 16.04) that permits SSH (22/tcp) and 8080/tcp while denying all other unrelated inbound traffic (default deny incoming, default allow outgoing). Verified the ruleset survives a full node reboot: ufw remains enabled/active, the INPUT chain policy stays DROP, and only 22/tcp and 8080/tcp are explicitly ACCEPTed, with loopback and ESTABLISHED/RELATED traffic allowed as usual. Completed the mandatory single-node restart evidence protocol: captured pre-reboot boot_id, triggered a native `sudo reboot`, confirmed the node went unreachable then came back with a changed boot_id and boot time, and re-verified firewall/service health post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (Ubuntu 16.04), confirmed ufw and iptables availability, and passwordless sudo
Captured pre-change baseline: ufw inactive, listening services (sshd on 22, systemd-resolve on 5355), sshd_config Port 22
Set ufw default deny incoming / allow outgoing; added allow rules for 22/tcp and 8080/tcp; enabled ufw

Verified systemd enablement (systemctl is-enabled/is-active ufw) and inspected iptables INPUT/ufw-before-input/ufw-user-input chains showing policy DROP with only 22/tcp and 8080/tcp explicitly accepted

Ran a same-host connectivity test to NODE_IP:8080/22/9999, discovered the test was invalid because traffic to the node's own IP routes via lo (which ufw unconditionally accepts), and instead relied on direct iptables rule inspection as valid evidence of enforcement for real external traffic on the ens2 interface
Cleaned up temporary nc test listeners
Captured pre-restart boot_id and boot time baseline plus ufw health
Triggered node1 reboot via backgrounded 'sleep 2 && sudo reboot' so the exec call acknowledged before disconnection
Polled node1 until command execution resumed, observing an intermediate 'connection refused' followed by successful exec with a changed boot_id and boot time, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified post-restart state: ufw enabled and active, default deny incoming policy intact, 22/tcp and 8080/tcp rules present, INPUT chain already showing dropped packets since boot

evidence.requirement: Persistent firewall permits SSH and TCP 8080 while denying other inbound traffic (post-configuration)
evidence.summary: ufw enabled with default deny incoming; iptables shows INPUT policy DROP and ufw-user-input only ACCEPTs tcp dpt:22 and tcp dpt:8080 on the real ens2 interface, with lo and ESTABLISHED/RELATED separately allowed

evidence.requirement: Firewall configuration is persistent (enabled at boot), not just active in the current session
evidence.summary: ufw enable output states 'Firewall is active and enabled on system startup'; systemctl is-enabled ufw confirms 'enabled' prior to restart
Captured boot_id fa1e87e6... and boot time 2026-09-29 10:58:43 with ufw active and rules for 22/tcp present, immediately before the restart

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returns before disconnection
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sleep 2 && sudo reboot' command acknowledged (exit 0) before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed after restart (proof of actual restart, not just elapsed time)
evidence.summary: Intermediate poll showed 'Connection refused' during reboot; subsequent poll succeeded with boot_id aa6782c3... and boot time 2026-09-29 11:00:07, both different from the pre-restart baseline

evidence.requirement: Node1 required services and firewall state recovered post-restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart check shows ufw enabled and active, default deny (incoming)/allow (outgoing), rules for 22/tcp and 8080/tcp intact, INPUT chain policy DROP already enforcing (3 packets dropped since boot), and sshd listening on 22 — successful exec itself proves SSH access survived the restart
